root_cause.text: The rename operations in shmem did not handle maple_tree insertion failures (e.g., due to memory pressure) properly, leaving directory offset structures inconsistent and lacking recovery after a successful shmem_whiteout.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that "maple_tree insertions can fail if we are seriously short on memory; simple_offset_rename() does not recover well if it runs into that. ... Moreover, shmem_whiteout() expects that if it succeeds, the caller will progress to d_move(), i.e. that shmem_rename2() won't fail past the successful call of shmem_whiteout()." The patch changes simple_offset_rename from returning an int (with possible failure) to void, and moves the guaranteed-to-succeed preinsertion of the new entry into the offset tree into shmem_rename2 before shmem_whiteout, ensuring later steps cannot fail. Similarly, simple_offset_rename_exchange is reworked to use mtree_store directly (which cannot fail on already-present indices) and to swap offsets only after successful stores.
